Jack's Cupboard

Email 605-688-4493
Free, On-Campus Food Pantry

Our goal is to alleviate food insecurity among SDSU students by providing food and personal care items to Jackrabbits who need them.

How it Works Additional Resources Volunteer Donate
Fall 2026

Hours: Tuesdays and Wednesdays from 3-6 p.m.

Location: Ben Reifel Hall (south side)

**Students can shop at Jack's Cupboard once a week. Items you get from the cupboard should supply you for a week.

Hours are subject to change due to weather, holiday breaks and at the beginning of a new semester. Check here for updates.

How it Works

  1. Bring your student ID and a reusable bag for your items to Jack's Cupboard in Ben Reifel Hall.
    • If you don't have a bag, you can request one at the front desk.
  2. Shop from the shelves.
    • Please only take what you would use for the week and follow any posted signs.
  3. Check out at the front desk when you are done.
    • You will be asked to scan your student ID, and a volunteer at the desk will weigh your items.

Once you have checked out, you're good to go!

First Come, First Served
No Saving Spots in Line

To keep your place in line, you must be physically present and waiting.

Personal belongings can't be used to reserve a spot in line.

If items are left outside of the Jack's Cupboard door to save a place in line, they will be moved inside and stored behind the desk. Please ask the volunteer on duty if you need help retrieving your belongings.

FAQ

Still have questions?

Contact Us
Who does Jack’s Cupboard serve and who is eligible?

Currently enrolled SDSU students.

When is Jack’s Cupboard open?

Hours are subject to change due to weather, holiday breaks and at the beginning of a new semester. Check the hours of operation for current hours.

What information is collected?
  • Student ID number
  • Household number
  • Age range
What items are offered?

It varies.

How can I donate?

Read more about how to donate and our various needs, including volunteers!

What is Cash Course? What is the access code?
  • Cash Course is a real-life money guide, helping students and staff learn how to earn, save, invest, protect, borrow and pay for their education.
  • Access code: 4627
  • To register:
    • Go to Cash Course Login.
    • Click Register Now.
    • Select Yes, I have a code and enter the four digit access code above.
    • Provide your name and email address.
    • Verify your account.
    • Pick a username. You can make up your own or use the prepopulated suggestion.
    • Click the Let's Get Started! play button.

Volunteer Opportunities
Link to Volunteer Sign-up
Volunteer Staff
Fall Semester

Students can volunteer for the fall semester at Jack's Cupboard. Volunteer responsibilities include assisting shoppers with checkout, distributing freezer items and items in the glass cabinet to shoppers and completing opening and closing tasks.

Volunteer Sign-up
Link to Contact Us
Host a Drive
All Year

Student organizations and community members can organize donation drives. If you plan to organize one, please let us know. We will answer your questions and coordinate a drop-off time for donations once your drive is complete.

Contact Us
Supporting Our Students
Monetary Donations

Staff, students and the Brookings Community can all help support our Jackrabbits facing food insecurity.

If you would like to make a monetary donation to Jack's Cupboard, you can do so online through the South Dakota State University Foundation.

Give to Jack's Cupboard
Food Donations

Please note:
Donated food must be prepackaged items that are shelf-stable or can be frozen.

Recommended Donation Items
  • Blocks of cheese, cream cheese and butter
  • Frozen products such as pizzas, frozen dinners and meat options
  • Canned soup or bagged soup mixes
  • Pasta and pasta sauces
  • Bread, rice and other grains
  • Evaporated, powdered and boxed milk
  • Canned fruits and vegetables
  • Dried fruits
  • Cereal and oatmeal
  • Canned chicken and canned tuna
  • Peanut butter and jelly
  • Condiments
  • Prepackaged snack items
  • Cake, brownie and pancake mixes
  • Baking items (baking soda, baking powder, salt, etc.)
  • Personal care items (toothbrushes, toothpaste, tampons, pads, shampoo, body wash, laundry detergent, toilet paper, etc.)
Where to Donate

Donations are accepted at:

  • Jack's Cupboard during normal hours of operation.
  • Housing and Residential Life Office weekdays from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • University Student Union during hours of operation.
  • University Police Department 24/7.

If you have a large donation, please contact sdsu.jackscupboard@sdstate.edu to set up a drop-off time.

Additional Resources

On Campus Resources
Food Recovery Network

Meals are available for pickup at Jack’s Cupboard during operating hours (Tuesdays and Wednesdays, 3-6 p.m.)

This nationally affiliated organization recovers leftover food from campus partners and donates it, diverting this food from the landfill.
Follow Food Recovery Network on Instagram
Swipe Out Hunger

If you are facing food insecurity and are short of block meals at Larson Commons, learn how you can either donate meal blocks or apply for additional meals through the Swipe Out Hunger program.

This program lasts all year.
Swipe Out Hunger
